title: canary-rollout-planning-scratchpad
content:
Quick notes / scratchpad for the upcoming canary rollout (hosted API: model variant v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0; Dedicated customers on reserved pools follow separate schedule).

Context:
- Goal: gradual rollout of runtime + model changes (improved attention kernel and quantization tweaks) with minimal customer impact and measurable cost/latency improvements.
- Risk areas: token-level regression (quality), P95 latency increase, backend OOMs on long-context requests, cache incompatibilities between v2.3.1 and v2.4.0 model binaries.

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Internal dev-only smoke (team members; feature-flagged) — today (DEV pool)
2) Canary stage A: 1% of production traffic routed -> new model variant & runtime flags (24h)
3) Canary stage B: 5% (48–72h) if stage A healthy
4) Canary stage C: 20% (72h)
5) Ramp to 50% / schedule maintenance window for Dedicated if metrics good
6) Full rollout + post-mortem

Canary cohort definition:
- Sampling: request-weight based (not user-based) for hosted API routes /v1/generate and /v1/chat.postMessage. Exclude internal admin and integration test keys.
- Cohort targets: 1%, 5%, 20%, 50%
- Exclusions: customers in enterprise-reserved capacity, experiments with pinned model_version, latency-sensitive SLAs (classify by tag)

Traffic control mechanism:
- Routing rule: feature flag + traffic router config (RouteID: canary-v2-2026-01)
- How to pin: customers with pinned model_version remain on v2.3.x (config read order currently: user pinned -> routing rules -> default)
- Rollback: flip feature flag to route 100% back to v2.3.1; automatic fallback policy already exists to route to nearest compatible variant on serve-time failures

What to monitor (primary metrics):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 request latency (token-incremental and total response time)
- Errors: 5xx rate (per-route), model inference errors, OOMs
- Cost: per-token GPU time, batch sizes (effective throughput), average tokens/request (to catch prompt inflation)
- Quality: automated eval set MRR/ROUGE/LLR on daily batch (we run eval job every 6 hours against canary responses)
- Regression checks: divergence on top-5 responses for 50 canonical prompts (we have the eval harness under runtime/tests/canary-evals)
- Alerts (initial thresholds): p95 increase > 25% over baseline OR error rate increase > 0.5% absolute -> page on-call SRE and release lead

Smoke tests (automated):
- Quick health checks: /health endpoints for all deploys
- End-to-end generation tests (10 canonical prompts) -> compare hashes + manual review if mismatch
- Long-context test (20k tokens) for memory regressions
- Streaming correctness: partial-chunk reconstructions
- Authentication checks: session tokens issued correctly

Manual checks (pre-1%):
- Verify model binary checksums and container images (sha256 recorded in release notes)
- Sanity run of canary-eval harness locally (Marco)
- Check KV cache compatibility (Priya) — if incompatible, ensure we flush pref. cache for canary cohort only

Version pinning notes (important):
- We must NOT override customer-model-version pin settings. Code path: routing -> read user.metadata.pinned_model_version -> if present, route to that variant. Double-check logic in routing service (PR #2784).
- For Dedicated customers: ops will coordinate offline upgrade windows (separate doc). Add note to Dedicated runbook to avoid auto-apply.

Fallback variants and compatibility:
- Fallback model: v2.3.1 (stable). Provide a pinned fallback flag on route config to ensure immediate fallback on runtime exception.
- Cache schema: v1 -> v2 migration: canary will use a new cache key prefix (canary-v240-<model-id>) to avoid reusing incompatible cache values. This increases upstream compute cost for canary but prevents corruption.

Runbook snippets / commands (placeholders):
- Rollout start: curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/route/update -d '{"route": "canary-v2-2026-01", "traffic_pct": 1}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- Rollback: curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/route/update -d '{"route": "canary-v2-2026-01", "traffic_pct": 0}'
- Check route status: internal-cli routes status canary-v2-2026-01 --json
- Tail canary logs: kubectl -n inference logs -l app=runtime-canary -f --since=2h | grep "ERROR"

Who needs to be paged (onsite escalation):
- oncall-sre@redwood (primary)
- eng-release (release lead: Dana Park)
- eng-serving-runtime (Marco Li)
- ml-infra (Priya Shah)

Communication plan:
- Pre-rollout Slack message to #eng-release and #sre 1h before each stage with explicit traffic % and rollback instructions
- Daily status update (short bullets) to #release-ops and PMs during rollout
- Post-rollout email summary + invite to 1hr post-mortem if anything > sev-2

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q1: Are there any existing A/B experiments that rely on exact token-level logits? If yes, need to opt them out. (Ethan to audit experiments platform)
- Q2: Can we reduce KV cache warmup cost by pre-seeding common prefixes for canary cohort? (Priya exploring)
- TODO: Add a quick script to toggle traffic pct via CLI (safe defaults + dry-run) — assign to Marco
- TODO: Add 50 canonical prompts list to this doc (under runtime/tests/canary-evals) and include expected outputs snapshot

Notes from last run (Nov 2025):
- Observed small p95 spike (~12%) for chat route when batching increased due to slower kernel selection under long-context. Resolved by pinning kernel for context > 8k. Consider same pin here.
- One Dedicated customer had pinned variant broken by auto-upgrade last time -> ensure ops checklist includes double-confirmation step.

Post-rollout verification (24–72h):
- Confirm cost per token improved (or at least not worse) within 10%
- Run extended quality checks on 5k user production samples (anonymized) and compare against baseline
- Confirm no increased rate of manual escalations to support (support ticket monitor)

Final: keep this doc lightweight. Will move to confluence/REL-Canary-Playbook once plan is locked. If anything obvious missing ping me.
